analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The head hunk (lines 956-1003) adds a paragraph on an excluded startup shape warmup (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup). The supplied base units cover lines 1-797 of the file, which the patch does not touch, so they serve as unchanged context. The patch excerpt is truncated and the head text is not supplied, so I could only review the visible portion.

The visible warmup text describes behavior and security-relevant bounds:
- The warmup uses synthetic prompts (a greedy 128-token probe, a solo prompt, and a served-width cell) and the artifact's default sampling.
- It is bounded by a 20-second wall budget and a three-try cap.
- It trains no rate or counter.
- It is excluded from calibration probes.

I found no sign that consumer plaintext (A-001) is involved. The text names no prefix-cache donation or SSD interaction, so T-041 is not touched on the visible lines. The warmup could in principle populate the prefix cache or affect TTFT measurements. That cannot be confirmed from a truncated documentation excerpt, and no code change is supplied. A later pass should confirm that warmup requests carry no cache scope, so they cannot donate to the SSD cache. It should also confirm that the warmup cannot starve real requests, covering T-029 and T-010 availability, and that the 20 s budget preempts correctly under load.

The base text covers Nemotron Super slot admission and prefix-cache scoping. It states that image requests are scoped to the authenticated tenant and that there are no cache receipts. This is unchanged and consistent with T-041 scope partitioning. I report no regression or threat-model invalidation. Because the patch excerpt is truncated, I set needs_deeper_review to true only for the unseen tail of the hunk.
